recognize_zh: 周邊血中可見數個中大型、核質比高的異常細胞，核染色質細緻並有明顯核仁，細胞質灰藍色無顆粒，部分核呈凹陷或腎形，是循環中的 BPDCN 母細胞；形態本身非特異，需流式確認 CD123/CD4/CD56。
features: Three medium-to-large atypical mononuclear cells with high-to-intermediate N:C ratio
Round to indented or kidney-shaped nuclei with finely dispersed chromatin
Pale gray-blue agranular cytoplasm, focally with small vacuoles near the nucleus
Background red cells largely unremarkable; a smudged platelet/cell fragment at the lower right
describe_en: The peripheral blood smear shows several circulating medium-to-large atypical mononuclear cells. These cells have finely dispersed chromatin, distinct nucleoli, round to indented or reniform nuclei, and a moderate amount of agranular gray-blue cytoplasm with occasional small vacuoles. No Auer rods or cytoplasmic granules are identified, and the red cells show no significant morphologic abnormality. The cells are morphologically consistent with blasts; in the context of a CD4+/CD56+/CD123+ phenotype, findings are consistent with peripheral blood involvement by blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm.

ddx.vs: Monocytic blasts often show fine azurophilic granules, folded nuclei and NSE/lysozyme positivity with CD14/CD11b expression, whereas BPDCN blasts are agranular, NSE-negative and bright CD123+.
Lymphoblasts typically have scant cytoplasm and express TdT with B- or T-lineage markers, unlike the lineage-negative CD123+/TCF4+ BPDCN cells.
Reactive lymphocytes have more condensed chromatin, abundant cytoplasm that scallops around red cells, and a spectrum of forms, rather than a uniform population with blastic chromatin and nucleoli.
Lymphoma cells tend to be more pleomorphic with deeply basophilic, often vacuolated cytoplasm and express mature B or T markers on flow.
